newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nedlloyd seen turning Q1 loss around in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Nedlloyd seen turning Q1 loss around in Q2.

text.p: Dutch shipping and transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd is expected to break even in the second quarter this year, turning the tide on a hefty loss sustained in the first, analysts said.

Analysts' forecasts for the second quarter range from a 14 million guilder ($6.8 million) loss to a 20 million profit, a clear improvement on the 45 million guilder loss in the first quarter. The consensus was for a slim five million guilder net profit.
The figures are due for release on Wednesday and should reveal an extraordinary gain from Nedlloyd's disposal in June of a 40 percent stake in Smit Internationale.
Analysts are looking for further early signs of benefits from the company's P&O Nedlloyd joint venture, although they said most would not be felt until later this year.

P&O Nedlloyd was formed at the end of 1996, when Nedlloyd and Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co merged their container shipping activities, saying synergy savings would be achieved in late 1997 and into 1998.
Nedlloyd has since said the savings were ahead of schedule and would exceed the $200 million original forecast.

"People are really focusing on the third and fourth quarter -- that's when most of the big projects (within the joint venture) are being implemented," said analyst Rene van Geffen at Van Lanschot Bankiers.
"But we saw a little of the impact in the first quarter and we may see some more in the second."
"We should see benefits from the tariff increases, introduced by P&O Nedlloyd on its Europe/Far East routes during the second quarter," Van Geffen said.
One of the main problems in the first quarter was a weak performance from the ocean shipping division, where earnings were hit by an eight percent year-on-year tariff erosion.
But Nedlloyd said then it expected cost savings in the sector to ensure profits for the whole of 1997.

Analyst Corne Zandbergen from Generale Bank is predicting a net loss of five million guilders in the second quarter and said P&O Nedlloyd's return to profit will boost the group's overall total. The joint venture contributed a 38 million guilder loss to Nedlloyd in the first quarter.
"Cost savings due to the combined operations and decreasing price pressures on major trades will have a positive impact on the results," he said.
